ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure shows the action potential of ventricular contractile cardiac muscle fibers; the membrane potential first rises rapidly to the depolarization level, then is maintained near 0 mV in a relatively long flat plateau, and only afterward falls back to the resting potential. The right figure shows ion permeability changing over time, in which Na+ permeability briefly increases, while changes such as Ca2+ are related to the longer plateau phase. Reasoning: The question asks how depolarization in cardiac muscle fibers during the action potential differs compared with skeletal muscle fibers. Depolarization in skeletal muscle action potentials is usually very brief, while the cardiac muscle action potential in the figure shows an obvious, relatively long-lasting plateau phase after depolarization. Therefore, the duration of depolarization in cardiac muscle fibers is longer.
